To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The use of a cascade architecture with a large number of LSTM networks, extracted from a single LSTM network, is a very efficient way to perform lexicon verification.

(1) the cascade of LSTM networks is an interesting architecture for handwriting recognition; (2) the cascade of networks extracted from a same LSTM network (the cohort) is an interesting architecture; (3) the cascade of the cohort of LSTM networks coupled with a lexica verification stage provides state-of-the-art recognition performance.

(i) we propose a cascade of LSTM networks, trained with a single dataset, that can be used as a replacement of the lexicon driven recognition; (ii) this cascade can be applied to any kind of recognition task, and can be trained on any kind of dataset; (iii) this cascade provides a new state of the art performance on the RIMES and IAM databases, and can deal with a very large lexicon; (iv) the proposed cascade is very fast to train
